About Riverwalk Dental Group — Your Family Dental Home

Welcome to Riverwalk Dental Group, a multi-specialty family dental practice serving Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter. Our practice welcomes new patients at all four locations, and our team provides care in English and Spanish. This page will help you get to know about Riverwalk Dental Group — our approach, our doctors, and what sets us apart.

Call Us at (772) 918-9034 Our Dental Philosophy

A Practice Built Around Complete Care

We believe dental care should be convenient, coordinated, and personal. That is why Riverwalk Dental Group brings together general dentists and specialists in one practice — so you do not have to drive to multiple offices for different treatments.

Specialty Collaboration

Specialists In-House — No Referrals Out

Most family dental practices refer patients to outside offices for root canals, gum surgery, or implants. At Riverwalk Dental Group, we have a periodontist and implant surgeon and an oral surgeon on our team. When you need a root canal, a gum graft, or a full-mouth restoration, you can receive that care right here. This means fewer appointments, less time away from work, and a care team that already knows your history.

In-House Multi-Specialty Team Lifetime Dentistry

Serving Families Across Every Stage of Life

From a child's first cleaning to seniors needing dentures or implant-supported replacements, our practice cares for patients at every age. Our general dentists handle routine checkups and fillings, while our specialists step in for more advanced needs. It is a seamless experience for the whole family.

Pediatric to Senior Care Expert Clinicians

Meet Our Dental Team

Our Doctors

Riverwalk Dental Group is led by founder Dr. Payal Chokshi alongside a diverse team of experienced clinicians. Each doctor brings their own training and personality to the practice, but they all share a commitment to gentle, thorough care. You can read full biographies and credentials on our Our Team page. A few highlights: Dr. Laya Gholami is a double board-certified periodontist and implant surgeon, and Dr. Alameri provides oral surgery and cosmetic care. This depth of expertise is rare in a single practice and makes our dental team across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter truly unique.

We offer sedation options for those who need extra help relaxing. Patients often tell us they leave feeling at ease — and that is exactly the experience we work to create.

Our Clinical Team

Meet Dr. Laya Gholami, Periodontist & Implant Surgeon

Periodontist & Implant Surgeon English All 4 Locations Find a Location Request an Appointment

Dr. Laya Gholami, periodontist at Riverwalk Dental Group, brings advanced specialty training and double board certification to every patient she sees. As an in-house periodontist and implant surgeon, she offers our patients across South Florida the convenience of receiving complex gum and implant care without leaving the practice. Dr. Gholami is known for taking time to explain treatment options in clear, warm language. New patients are always welcome.

Find a Location Clinical Background

Education, Training & Board Certifications

Dr. Gholami completed an intensive residency in periodontics and implant surgery, followed by board certification in both specialties. She stays current with the latest evidence based techniques to ensure her patients receive care that is both effective and comfortable. Her double board certification means she has met rigorous national standards in periodontal disease management and surgical implant placement.

Global Perspective

Research & Academic Contributions

Beyond her clinical work, Dr. Gholami has contributed to periodontal research and academic literature. She brings this foundation of knowledge into every consultation, helping patients understand not just what treatment is recommended, but why it works. This depth of expertise is part of what makes the Riverwalk Dental Group team so well rounded.

Comprehensive Surgical & Restorative Care Est. 2012 Specialized Practice

Specialty Areas & Clinical Focus

Periodontal Care & Gum Disease Treatment

Gum disease affects more than just your smile: it has been linked to heart health, diabetes, and overall wellness. Dr. Gholami offers non-surgical and surgical periodontal treatment to stop the progression of gum disease and restore the health of your gums and supporting bone. Her goal is to help you keep your natural teeth for a lifetime. To learn more about gum health, visit our periodontics page.

Advanced Implant Surgery & Full-Mouth Rehabilitation

When one or more teeth are missing, dental implants are the closest replacement to natural teeth. Dr. Gholami plans and places implants with precision, using 3D imaging to ensure ideal positioning. Dental care can be costly, and simple procedures can even run up your bill. Caring for your teeth is necessary to keep your oral and general health in check. Many people have no dental benefits at all, or if they retire their benefits are lost. Skipping dental care is not an option, and can lead to other more serious health issues such as diabetes, or heart conditions. There are ways you can reduce your dental care costs, and help pay for those costly procedures that are necessary to keep your teeth and gums healthy.

Ask Your Dentist if They Offer an In-House Membership Plan

Many dental practices today offer their own dental membership for patients. These plans act like an insurance plan, and give patients discounts on procedures that are done in their office. If a patient does not have insurance it is wise to inquire about an in-house plan to help keep costs down.

Sign Up for a Dental Plan Through Your Employer

Many companies offer both medical and dental insurance plans. Most plans pay for at least half of the cost, and preventative services are typically covered 100 percent. Routine procedures are usually covered around 80 percent, and larger more involved procedures such as crowns are usually covered at 50 percent. Using in-network providers can help you save money, and allow you to get the dental work you need.

Dental Savings Plan

Dental savings plans are available to participants who pay a fee to join. The fee is typically annual, and allows you to choose from a network of dentists that offer discounts for members. Dental savings plans allow patients to get the work done that they need at a discounted price without insurance.

Affordable Care Act

Patients can apply for health insurance through the Affordable Care Act. Logging on to their website can let you know if you qualify to purchase dental coverage.

Dental HMO Plan

A dental HMO plan may be available in your state. Typically cleanings and exams twice a year are covered, and procedures are at a discount. Many dentists participate and accept HMO plans, and this is a good way to help save on dental care.

Veterans Benefits

If you are a veteran you qualify to receive insurance at a reduced rate. Disabled veterans are also eligible for free dental care through the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Do Your Research

If you are required to have a costly procedure, research the average price of that procedure. Ask your dentist for a discount, and most likely they will work with you, and help find a price and payment plan that fits your needs.

Create an Emergency Dental Fund

Setting aside money each month for dental care can help cover procedures or emergencies that are unpredictable. Knowing you have a savings account will put you at ease if an emergency arises and you need dental care.

Looking for an Affordable Dentist Near You?

Taking care of your oral health is a great way to prevent costly dental procedures. Brushing and flossing each day, and staying away from foods and drinks that contain sugar can help keep your teeth and gums healthy. Visiting our office regularly for exams and cleanings is extremely important to maintain your oral health. Regular visits allow our team to get in front of issues before they become urgent, and we can help you keep your teeth and mouth looking and feeling great.

We care about our patients, and our team is here to help take care of your oral health. Ask our team if you have questions on coverage or payment plans, and we will work with you to ensure you can receive the very best care.

To find out more about dental programs we offer, or to schedule your next dental exam, contact our office and our friendly staff will be happy to assist you.

If you have a dental crown or are considering one, you are probably wondering, how long do dental crowns last? At Riverwalk Dental Group, our experienced multi-specialty team provides customized crown care for patients of all ages across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter. We accept a wide range of insurance plans and offer patient-friendly financing options. And our approach is always patient-first, which means we take the time to explain your treatment options and help you make the best choice for your smile.

What Is the Average Lifespan of a Dental Crown?

Most dental crowns last between 5 and 15 years, but with proper care and the right material choice, many patients enjoy their crowns for 20 years or more. Your Riverwalk dentist will evaluate your specific situation to give you a more personalized estimate. The key factors are the material used, your oral hygiene habits, and how well you care for your crown day to day.

How Crown Material Affects How Long It Lasts

Different crown materials have different strengths and weaknesses. Your choice will affect the dental crown lifespan as well as the look and feel of your restoration.

Porcelain vs. Zirconia vs. Metal Crowns — Durability Compared

FeaturePorcelainZirconiaMetal
Average lifespan5–10 years10–15+ years15–20+ years
DurabilityModerate — prone to chipping or cracking under forceHigh — very strong and fracture-resistantHighest — extremely strong, resists wear and fracture
AestheticsExcellent — natural tooth color and translucencyGood — tooth-colored but can appear opaquePoor — metallic color, not suitable for visible teeth
Best use caseFront teeth where appearance matters mostMolars and premolars where strength is neededBack teeth (molars) where strength is critical and appearance is less of a concern

Porcelain crowns offer the most natural appearance, which is important for front teeth. Zirconia crowns combine strength with a tooth-like color, making them a popular choice for back teeth. Metal crowns (often gold alloy) are extremely durable but are almost always used on molars because of their color. Your dentist will help you choose the material that fits your needs and budget.

Factors That Affect How Durable Your Dental Crown Is

Your crown’s lifespan depends on more than just the material. Habits and the quality of your dental care play a big role.

Habits That Shorten Crown Life

  • •Grinding or clenching your teeth (bruxism) puts excessive force on the crown and can cause it to crack or wear down.
  • •Chewing hard objects like ice, pens, or popcorn kernels can chip or fracture the crown.
  • •Poor oral hygiene allows plaque to build up at the crown margin, leading to decay underneath or gum disease.
  • •Using your teeth as tools (opening packages, ripping tags) risks damaging the crown.
  • •Skipping dental checkups means small problems go unnoticed until the crown is compromised.

What Your Dentist Does to Help Crowns Last Longer

Your restorative dentist plays a crucial role in crown longevity. At Riverwalk Dental Group, our multi-specialty team takes careful impressions (often using digital scans) to ensure a precise fit. A well fitted crown has a tight seal that prevents bacteria from getting underneath. We also check your bite and adjust the crown so it meets opposing teeth evenly, reducing stress and wear. By including a periodontist and endodontists on our team, we can treat any underlying gum or root issues before placing the crown, which protects its foundation.

Dental Crown Care Tips to Maximize Longevity

Taking care of your crown is similar to caring for your natural teeth. Follow these dental crown care tips to help your crown last as long as possible:

  • •Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and floss once a day. Use floss threaders or interdental brushes if your crown has tight contacts.
  • •Pay special attention to the gumline where the crown meets your tooth. Plaque tends to collect there.
  • •Use a mouthguard if you grind your teeth at night. We can create a custom guard that fits over your crown.
  • •Avoid chewing on ice, hard candy, or other hard objects.
  • •Visit us regularly for cleanings and exams. We will check the crown’s fit, look for signs of wear, and take X-rays as needed to check the tooth underneath.
  • •If the crown feels loose or uncomfortable, call us right away. Early intervention can often save the crown.
Book Online

When Should You Replace a Dental Crown?

Crowns do not last forever. Even with perfect care, the cement seal can break down over time, or the tooth underneath may develop decay. Common signs that replacement is needed include:

  • •Chipping, cracking, or visible wear on the crown surface.
  • •Pain or sensitivity when chewing or to temperature changes.
  • •The crown feels loose or wiggles slightly.
  • •Dark lines appear at the gumline, which may indicate the cement has worn away or the metal underneath is showing.
  • •Food gets trapped around the crown, a sign the fit has changed.

If you notice any of these, schedule an exam. Replacing a failing crown early can prevent damage to the tooth underneath and save you more extensive treatment later. Across our offices across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter, we have general dentists and specialists who can evaluate and replace crowns efficiently.

How Successful Are Dental Implants?

Implants have a 95% success rate, and we encourage patients to use good oral hygiene habits to keep the implants clean and free of plaque. If an implant shifts out of place this could indicate the bone tissue is not providing enough support, and you should contact our dental office immediately.

Tips to Ensure your Dental Implants Last a Lifetime

Here are some helpful tips that you can start using to get the most out of your dental implants:

  • •Floss daily using an implant specific floss or wax free floss to help keep the area clean and free of plaque. A Waterpik Water Flosser can be used to assist in removing plaque around the implants.
  • •Use a low abrasive tooth brush such as a soft type brush on your implants.
  • •Avoid any products, foods, or drinks containing any ingredients that may stain your teeth.
  • •Anti-microbial rinses can be used to help reduce inflammation and prevent infection.
  • •Avoid products that contain stannous fluoride, sodium fluoride, or baking soda. These ingredients can make the implants prone to corrosion.

One of the most common questions patients ask us at Riverwalk Dental Group is, "is invisalign better than braces?" It's a big decision, and the answer depends on your personal goals, your smile, and your lifestyle. We welcome new patients at all four of our convenient locations across South Florida. Consultations are available in English and Spanish, so you can ask your questions in the language you're most comfortable with. Our experienced team is here to walk you through every option.

How Invisalign and Traditional Braces Work

Both Invisalign and braces move teeth into better alignment, but they do it differently.

How Clear Aligners Straighten Teeth

Invisalign uses a series of custom made, clear plastic aligners. Each set is worn for about two weeks, then switched to the next. The aligners apply gentle pressure to shift teeth gradually. You remove them to eat, brush, and floss. Most people never notice you're wearing them.

How Traditional Braces Work

Braces use metal or ceramic brackets bonded to each tooth, connected by a wire. The wire is tightened at regular appointments to guide teeth into position. Rubber bands may be added to correct bite issues. Braces are fixed in place for the entire treatment period.

Invisalign vs. Braces — Side-by-Side Comparison

Choosing between clear aligners and braces comes down to what matters most to you. Here's a simple comparison to help you weigh the differences.

FeatureInvisalign (Clear Aligners)Traditional Braces
VisibilityNearly invisible when wornNoticeable metal or tooth colored brackets
RemovabilityRemovable for eating and cleaningFixed on teeth until treatment ends
ComfortSmooth plastic, no sharp edgesBrackets and wires can irritate cheeks and gums
Treatment Duration12 to 18 months on average18 to 24 months or more for complex cases
Maintenance / CleaningRemove to brush and floss normallyRequires special flossing and food restrictions
Cost RangeTypically comparable to braces (varies by case)Similar range, includes additional adjustments
Case ComplexityBest for mild to moderate crowding or gapsSuited for severe misalignment, bite problems, and rotations
Adult SuitabilityVery popular among adults due to discretionAlso effective for adults; some prefer clear ceramic brackets

Is Invisalign or Braces Better for Adults?

Adults often prefer Invisalign because the aligners are clear and removable. You can eat whatever you like, brush normally, and smile in photos without feeling self conscious. For many, the answer to "is invisalign better than braces" comes down to lifestyle. However, if your case involves significant bite issues, rotated teeth, or a large gap, traditional braces may deliver a more predictable result.

Request an Appointment

Which Option Is Right for You?

The only way to know for sure is a consultation with a dental professional. At Riverwalk Dental Group, we evaluate your teeth, gums, and goals to recommend the best path. We also offer sedation dentistry if you're nervous about any part of the process. Your smile journey should feel comfortable and clear every step of the way.

If you're still weighing your options, you might also be interested in our cosmetic dentistry services — including veneers and smile makeovers — which can address other concerns like color, shape, and chips alongside alignment.

Common Dental Emergencies

Why Patients across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter Choose Invisalign at Riverwalk Dental Group

People choose Invisalign because it fits comfortably into daily life. The smooth plastic trays are nearly invisible, so you can straighten your smile without the look of metal braces. You can remove them to eat, brush, and floss — no food restrictions, no extra cleaning steps. That freedom makes a real difference for adults balancing work and family and for teens who want a low-profile option.

Invisalign also offers flexibility. Whether you need to fix mild crowding, close small gaps, or correct a bite issue, the treatment plan is customized to your smile. And since Riverwalk Dental Group provides a full range of cosmetic and specialty care, you get complete support in one place. We also offer complementary services like cosmetic dentistry and teeth whitening to complete your look.

What to Expect From Your Invisalign Treatment

Getting started with Invisalign is straightforward. You begin with a consultation where one of our dentists examines your teeth, discusses your goals, and maps out a digital treatment plan. From there, a series of custom aligner trays is made just for you. You wear each set for about two weeks, then switch to the next, gradually moving your teeth into their ideal positions.

Check-in visits every four to six weeks let our team track your progress and make sure everything is on schedule. Most treatments last 12 to 18 months, but timing depends on the complexity of your case. We make scheduling easy with convenient appointment times at any of our offices across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter.

Invisalign vs. Traditional Braces — Which Is Right for You?

If you're comparing your options, here's how clear aligners and traditional braces stack up:

RemovabilityRemovable for eating/brushingFixed

Invisalign is often the right fit for people with mild to moderate alignment issues who want discretion and convenience. Braces can be a better choice for more complex or severe cases. Our team will help you weigh the tradeoffs and choose the approach that fits your needs. For a deeper comparison, read our blog post Is Invisalign Better Than Braces?.

Who Is a Good Candidate for Invisalign?

Invisalign works for adults and teens with mild to moderate crowding, gaps between teeth, or minor bite issues. The best way to find out if you're a candidate is to come in for a consultation. At Riverwalk Dental Group, we assess your teeth and bite to see if clear aligners can deliver the results you want. Many people who thought braces were their only option are surprised by what Invisalign can do.

We also offer veneers for patients looking for faster shape and color changes, and our insurance and financing options make treatment accessible.

Why Choose Professional Teeth Whitening?

Over-the-counter whitening products can be tempting, but they often fall short of your expectations. Professional teeth whitening at our practice offers key advantages:

  • •Strength: We use professional-grade bleaching agents that lift deep stains far more effectively than drugstore strips or trays.
  • •Speed: Most patients achieve multiple shades of improvement in a single, hour long visit.
  • •Safety: Your treatment is supervised by a dentist who protects your gums and ensures the gel is applied correctly.
  • •Personalization: We match the whitening shade to your natural tooth color and your desired brightness for a result that looks natural, not overdone.

Our team will discuss your goals and recommend the approach that fits your lifestyle, whether you want dramatic improvement quickly or a gradual touch-up at home.

What to Expect During Your Whitening Visit

Your whitening appointment starts with a consultation and a careful shade assessment. We clean your teeth, apply a protective barrier to your gums, then apply the whitening gel. A special light may be used to accelerate the process. After the gel sits for the prescribed time, it is removed and your new shade is checked. The entire visit takes about 60 to 90 minutes, and you walk out with a noticeably brighter smile.

Throughout the process, we check in on your comfort. If you have any sensitivity, we can adjust the treatment to keep you at ease.

In-Office Whitening vs. Take-Home Whitening Kits

Not sure which option is right for you? The table below compares the two approaches:

SupervisionDentist-supervisedSelf-applied

If you want the quickest, most dramatic change, in-office whitening is the way to go. If you prefer to whiten gradually at home, we can provide professional take-home trays with gel customized for your teeth.

Is Teeth Whitening Right for You?

Teeth whitening works best for surface stains from coffee, tea, wine, and tobacco. Deeper discoloration from medication or injury may need a different approach, such as veneers or bonding. During your consultation, we will examine your teeth and discuss your stain type to make sure whitening is a good fit.

Patients with sensitive teeth can still whiten safely. We use desensitizing agents and tailor the gel concentration and application time to your needs. Our goal is to give you a brighter smile without unnecessary discomfort.

What Are Porcelain Veneers? (And Are They Right for You?)

Porcelain veneers are thin layers of dental ceramic bonded to the front of your teeth. Each veneer is custom crafted in a dental lab to match your natural tooth color and shape. They are a popular choice for people who want a long lasting cosmetic improvement without major dental work. Dr. Ariana Romero Guerra and Dr. Alameri have experience creating smile makeovers that feel personal and look completely natural.

Conditions Veneers Can Address

Veneers can address a range of cosmetic concerns, including:

  • •Chipped or worn edges
  • •Stubborn discoloration that whitening cannot fix
  • •Small gaps between teeth
  • •Teeth that are misshapen or slightly uneven

If you have healthy teeth and gums, you are likely a good candidate. During a consultation, we will evaluate your smile and talk through your goals.

Veneers vs. Dental Bonding — Which Is the Better Fit?

Dental bonding uses a tooth colored resin applied directly to your teeth. It is a faster, less expensive option but may not last as long. The table below compares the two treatments.

FeaturePorcelain VeneersDental Bonding
Durability10 to 15 years with proper care3 to 7 years
Cost rangeHigher upfront investmentMore affordable initially
Stain resistanceHighly resistant to stainingMore prone to staining over time
Preparation requiredThin layer of enamel removedMinimal to no enamel removal
Ideal candidateLooking for a long term, dramatic changeQuick fix for small chips or shape adjustments

If you are deciding between the two, consider how long you want the result to last and how much change you are looking for. Veneers offer a more permanent solution, while bonding is a good short term option. Learn more about dental bonding to see which fits your situation.

The Benefits of Choosing Porcelain Veneers

Porcelain veneers do more than cover imperfections. They restore your natural smile and the confidence that goes with it.

  • •Natural appearance. Porcelain mimics the light reflecting properties of natural tooth enamel, so your smile looks real.
  • •Stain resistance. Coffee, tea, and other common stains do not easily penetrate glazed porcelain.
  • •Longevity. With regular care, veneers can last more than a decade.
  • •Minimal tooth removal. Only a thin layer of enamel is removed, preserving more of your natural tooth structure.
  • •Confidence boost. Many patients tell us they smile more freely and feel like themselves again.

What to Expect: Your Veneer Journey at Riverwalk Dental Group

Getting veneers usually takes two to three visits spread over a few weeks. We make sure you know what is happening at every step.

Consultation and Digital Smile Design Preview

Your first visit is a conversation. We look at your teeth, discuss what you want to change, and take images or scans. Using digital smile design, we show you a preview of how your new smile could look. You can see the potential result before any work begins. This step helps you feel confident about moving forward.

Veneer Placement — Step by Step

On your next visit, we prepare your teeth by gently removing a thin layer of enamel. Impressions are sent to a dental lab where your custom veneers are made. Temporary veneers protect your teeth while you wait. At the final appointment, we bond each veneer in place and make sure the fit and shade are perfect.

What Happens If You Leave Cosmetic Concerns Untreated?

This is not about fear. It is simply worth knowing that some cosmetic concerns can change over time. Chipped edges may wear further. Gaps can trap food and make cleaning harder. Stains that bother you today might deepen. More importantly, if you feel self conscious about your smile, that feeling often grows. Addressing these concerns now can prevent extra work later and let you enjoy your smile sooner.

Why Patients Choose Riverwalk for Their Smile Makeover

We hear from patients who have looked at other practices and chose us for a few clear reasons.

  • •Experienced doctors. Our team includes general dentists with a focus on cosmetics, like Dr. Ariana Romero Guerra and Dr. Alameri, who bring years of hands on experience.
  • •Multilingual care. We speak English and Spanish, so you can communicate comfortably.
  • •Complete care under one roof. From cosmetic enhancements to restorative treatments, you can get everything you need without referrals.
  • •Sedation options. If you feel nervous about dental work, we offer sedation to help you relax.

We also accept many insurance plans and offer flexible financing. Check our insurance and financing page for details.

All-on-4 is a full-arch implant system that uses just four strategically placed implants to support a fixed bridge of replacement teeth. The procedure involves placing two implants at the front of the jaw and two at an angle in the back, maximizing contact with available bone. What Is a Dental Bone Graft and Who Needs One?

A dental bone graft is a procedure that adds bone or bone-like material to an area of the jaw where bone has thinned or deteriorated. It creates a stronger, thicker foundation for dental implants. People who have been missing teeth for a while, have gum disease, or have experienced bone loss from injury or infection are often candidates for a graft. The goal is to restore enough bone so that implants can be placed securely.

Bone Grafting vs. Skipping Bone Grafting: What Patients Should Know

Choosing to have a bone graft before implants makes a clear difference in your treatment options and long-term results. Here is what you need to know:

FeatureWith Bone GraftingWithout Bone Grafting
Implant eligibilityRestored in most casesMay be denied outright
Long-term implant stabilityHighAt risk due to insufficient bone
Jawbone preservationActively rebuiltContinued deterioration
Treatment pathwayMulti-phase, plannedLimited to non-implant options
Candidacy for All-on-4Often achievableMay be excluded

If you are considering dental implants or All-on-4 implants, a bone graft may be the step that makes those treatments possible. Our implant dentistry team can guide you through the process.

What to Expect From Your Bone Grafting Treatment

We design each treatment plan around your unique needs. Here is a general overview of what your journey may look like.

Your Consultation and Imaging

Your first visit includes a thorough exam and cone beam CT scan to measure your jawbone density. This imaging helps Dr. Gholami plan the precise location and type of graft you need. We will walk through your options and answer every question before moving forward.

The Grafting Procedure

On the day of the procedure, you will receive local anesthesia to keep you comfortable. Depending on your needs, we may recommend sedation dentistry to help you relax. Dr. Gholami places the graft material in the targeted area and then closes the site with small stitches. The procedure itself usually takes about an hour.

Recovery and Healing Timeline

After your graft, you can expect some mild swelling and tenderness for a few days. Most patients return to normal activities within 48 hours. The graft needs time to fuse with your existing bone, which typically takes three to six months. Once healing is complete, we will move forward with placing your implant. Our team will check in with you at every stage to ensure your recovery stays on track.

Why a Dental Implant Is the Gold Standard for a Missing Tooth

Dental implants have become the most recommended option for replacing a single missing tooth because they replace the entire tooth structure — both the visible crown and the root. This makes them different from other solutions like bridges or partial dentures.

What Makes an Implant-Supported Crown Different From a Bridge or Denture

The table below compares the three main options for replacing a single missing tooth. Each has its own pros and cons, but the implant stands out for its long-term health benefits.

FeatureSingle Tooth ImplantDental BridgePartial Denture
Bone preservationPreserves jawbone by stimulating natural bone growthDoes not prevent bone loss; bone may shrink over timeDoes not prevent bone loss
Longevity10 to 15 years or longer with proper care5 to 10 years typically3 to 5 years on average
Adjacent tooth impactNo impact on healthy neighboring teethRequires filing down adjacent teeth for supportClasps can wear on neighboring teeth over time
MaintenanceBrush and floss normally; no special cleaningRequires special flossing under the bridgeMust remove for cleaning; can trap food
Cost range (single tooth)Higher initial cost but often more cost-effective long-termModerate initial costLower initial cost but needs frequent replacement

As you can see, a single tooth implant offers the best long-term value because it protects your bone and leaves your other teeth untouched.

What Happens If You Leave a Missing Tooth Untreated

When a missing tooth is not replaced, the surrounding teeth can shift into the gap. This can cause bite problems, make cleaning harder, and increase your risk of decay and gum disease. More importantly, the jawbone under the missing tooth begins to shrink because it no longer receives stimulation from the tooth root. Over time, bone loss can make future implant placement more complicated. Replacing the tooth early with a single tooth implant helps you avoid these complications and keeps your smile healthy.

What to Expect: Your Single Tooth Implant Process at Riverwalk Dental

We make the process of getting a single tooth implant across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter as straightforward and comfortable as possible. Here is what you can expect from start to finish.

Step 1 — Consultation and CT Imaging

Your first visit includes a thorough exam and a cone beam CT scan. This 3D image allows Dr. Gholami to see the exact shape and density of your jawbone, plan the ideal implant position, and check whether any bone grafting is needed before placement. We also discuss your goals, review your insurance benefits, and provide a clear cost estimate.

Step 2 — Implant Placement and Healing

During the implant placement procedure, Dr. Gholami surgically inserts a small titanium post into your jawbone. This post serves as the new tooth root. The procedure is done under local anesthesia, and we offer sedation options if you feel anxious. After placement, the implant needs time to fuse with the bone — a process called osseointegration. This typically takes three to four months. A temporary tooth may be placed to keep your smile looking natural during healing.

Step 3 — Your Custom Implant-Supported Crown

Once the implant has fully integrated, we take digital impressions and craft a custom crown that matches the shape, size, and color of your surrounding teeth. The crown is then securely attached to the implant. You leave with a fully functional, natural-looking tooth that feels just like the real thing.

What makes our implant program different is the level of expertise you get under one roof. Dr. Laya Gholami is a double board-certified periodontist and implant surgeon with advanced training in bone augmentation and full-mouth rehabilitation. What Is Gum Grafting?

Gum grafting is a periodontal procedure that adds tissue to areas where the gumline has receded and exposed the tooth root. Recession can happen for several reasons, including brushing too hard, untreated gum disease, teeth grinding, or simply genetics. Left alone, exposed roots are more vulnerable to sensitivity, decay, and further bone loss.

Types of Gum Grafts We Offer

Graft TypeWhere Tissue Comes FromBest For
Connective tissue graftBeneath a flap of tissue from the roof of the mouthThe most common type, used for moderate to significant recession
Free gingival graftA thin layer of tissue from the roof of the mouthPatients with thin gum tissue who need added thickness
Pedicle graftGum tissue adjacent to the recession sitePatients with plenty of healthy gum tissue near the affected tooth

What Happens If Gum Recession Goes Untreated

As recession progresses, more of the tooth root becomes exposed, increasing sensitivity to hot, cold, and sweet foods. Exposed roots are also softer than enamel, making them more prone to decay. Over time, untreated recession can contribute to bone loss around the tooth and, in advanced cases, tooth loss. Addressing recession early with gum grafting is a far simpler treatment than managing its complications later.

Your Gum Grafting Process at Riverwalk Dental

Step 1. Consultation and Evaluation

Dr. Gholami examines the extent of your recession, measures the affected areas, and identifies the likely cause. We discuss which graft type is right for your case and review your options for sedation.

Step 2. The Grafting Procedure

Depending on the graft type, Dr. Gholami takes tissue from the roof of your mouth or nearby gum tissue and secures it over the exposed root. The procedure is done under local anesthesia.

Step 3. Healing and Aftercare

Most patients heal within one to two weeks, with soft food recommended during the first several days. Dr. Gholami will give you specific aftercare instructions to protect the graft while it integrates.

Implant-supported dentures combine the stability of dental implants with the familiar look of a denture. Instead of resting on your gums alone, your denture attaches to two or more implants placed in your jawbone. This keeps the denture from shifting while you eat or speak, and it helps slow the bone loss that comes with wearing a traditional denture.

What Is Ridge Augmentation?

Ridge augmentation is a bone grafting procedure focused specifically on the alveolar ridge, the bony ledge that holds your tooth roots. After a tooth is lost or extracted, this ridge can resorb, becoming too narrow or too short to safely anchor an implant. During ridge augmentation, Dr. Gholami adds bone graft material to the ridge and allows it to heal and integrate before implant placement.

Ridge Augmentation vs. Other Bone Grafting Procedures

FeatureRidge AugmentationGeneral Bone GraftingSinus Lift
Where it's performedThe horizontal ridge where a tooth is missingVarious sites depending on the defectThe upper jaw near the sinus floor
What it addressesNarrow or collapsed ridge width and heightA range of bone loss causesInsufficient bone height in the upper back jaw
Common candidatesPatients with a long-missing toothPatients with bone loss from injury or diseasePatients needing upper back implants

What Happens If You Skip Ridge Augmentation

Without enough ridge width or height, an implant may not have adequate bone to anchor into, which can lead to implant instability or failure. In some cases, placing an implant into an inadequate ridge can also leave the implant visible under thin gum tissue. Addressing the ridge first protects your investment in a long-term, stable result.

Your Ridge Augmentation Process at Riverwalk Dental

Step 1. Evaluation and CT Imaging

A cone beam CT scan lets Dr. Gholami measure the exact width and height of your ridge and determine how much grafting is needed before implant placement.

Step 2. The Ridge Augmentation Procedure

Dr. Gholami places bone graft material along the ridge, using your own bone, donor bone, or a synthetic substitute depending on your case. The site is closed and given time to heal.

Step 3. Healing and Implant Placement

Ridge augmentation typically needs four to six months to fully integrate before an implant can be placed. Once healing is confirmed, we move forward with your implant procedure.

Why Patients Choose Sedation Dentistry

For many people, the thought of sitting in a dental chair brings real stress. Sedation dentistry removes that barrier. It allows you to get treatment without fear or discomfort. Patients who choose sedation often say they feel calm, safe, and able to complete procedures they had been putting off.

Who Is a Good Candidate for Dental Sedation?

You are a good candidate if you have mild to severe dental anxiety, a strong gag reflex, or trouble sitting still for long periods. People with sensitive teeth, a low pain tolerance, or past negative dental experiences also benefit from sedation. Even if you just want a more relaxed visit, sedation may be right for you. Your dentist will review your health history and recommend the best option.

What Happens If Dental Anxiety Goes Untreated?

Putting off care because of fear can lead to worse problems. Small cavities turn into larger ones, gum disease worsens, and teeth may need extraction. Avoiding the dentist also means missing early detection of issues that could become painful or costly. Sedation helps you stay on top of your oral health without the worry.

Your Sedation Options at Riverwalk Dental Group

We offer two safe, effective forms of sedation. Each is designed to help you feel at ease during your visit.

Nitrous Oxide (Laughing Gas)

Nitrous oxide is a mild sedative you breathe through a small mask placed over your nose. It works within minutes and creates a light, floating feeling. You remain fully awake and aware. Once the procedure is done, the gas wears off quickly so you can drive yourself home.

Oral Sedation

Oral sedation involves taking a pill about an hour before your appointment. The medication helps you reach a deeper level of relaxation. You stay awake but may feel drowsy and less aware of the treatment. Because the effects last longer, you will need someone to drive you home.

Nitrous Oxide vs. Oral Sedation — Which Is Right for You?

The table below compares the two options so you can see what fits your needs.

FeatureNitrous OxideOral Sedation
How it's administeredInhaled through a maskPill taken before appointment
Onset timeMinutes30–60 minutes before visit
Sedation depthMild relaxationModerate sedation
Recovery timeRapid — drive yourself homeExtended — escort required
Best forMild anxiety, short proceduresModerate-to-severe anxiety, longer visits
Available at this practiceYesYes

Your dentist will help you decide which option suits you best based on your anxiety level, the type of procedure, and your personal preference.

What to Expect at Your Sedation Appointment

Knowing what happens before, during, and after sedation can help you feel more prepared and confident.

Before Your Visit

Your dentist will review your medical history and any medications you take. If you choose oral sedation, you will receive the pill and instructions on when to take it. Arrange for a ride home if needed. You may also be asked to avoid eating for a few hours before your appointment.

During Your Procedure

Once you are in the chair, the sedation begins. For nitrous oxide, you breathe the gas through the mask. For oral sedation, the medication is already working. Our team monitors you the entire time, adjusting sedation levels as needed. Most patients feel comfortable and at ease, and many do not remember the procedure afterward.

After Sedation — Recovery and Next Steps

If you received nitrous oxide, you can resume normal activities right away. After oral sedation, you should rest for the remainder of the day. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or making important decisions for at least 24 hours. We will give you clear aftercare instructions based on your treatment.

Sedation Dentistry for Implant Procedures

If you are considering dental implants, sedation can make the process much more comfortable. Many implant procedures involve multiple steps, and being relaxed throughout helps you avoid stress. Our implant dentistry team works closely with patients who choose sedation for single implants, All-on-4 implants, and full-mouth restorations. We also offer bone grafting when needed to support the implant. Learn more about how our Implant Dentistry services combine advanced care with patient comfort.

Why Your Dentist Recommends a CT Scan

A dental CT scan goes beyond what standard X-rays can show. It gives your dentist a complete three-dimensional view of your teeth, jawbone, nerves, and sinuses. This level of detail is critical for planning treatments like implants, root canals, and surgical extractions.

What Is a Cone Beam CT Scan?

A cone beam CT scan uses a specialized X-ray machine that rotates around your head, capturing hundreds of images in one pass. The result is a 3D model your dentist can rotate, zoom, and measure. This technology gives a cone beam CT scan dentist the ability to assess bone density, locate infection, and plan surgery with greater confidence.

Image type3D volume (cross-sectional views)2D flat image
Detail levelShows bone, nerves, sinuses in three dimensionsShows tooth structure and basic bone outlines
Radiation exposureLow dose, similar to a standard dental panoramicLower dose for individual films
Use casesImplant planning, root canal evaluation, bone grafting assessment, impacted teethCavity detection, routine checkups, bitewing exams
Who benefits mostPatients needing surgery, complex restorations, or advanced diagnosticsPatients for routine preventive care

A CT scan gives your dentist deeper insight than a traditional X-ray. It is recommended when precise anatomical information is needed for your care. Our technology includes a cone beam CT scanner designed for patient comfort and safety.

Over time, untreated gum disease and decay can lead to tooth loss and restorative treatment that costs more than simple cleanings. What Is Dental Bonding?

Dental bonding is a cosmetic and restorative treatment that uses a tooth-colored resin to repair minor imperfections. Your dentist carefully shapes and polishes the material to match your natural teeth, making it ideal for:

  • •Chipped or cracked teeth
  • •Gaps between teeth
  • •Discolored or stained enamel
  • •Slightly misshapen teeth

Because the resin bonds directly to your tooth, no enamel removal is needed. It’s a gentle option that preserves your natural structure. For more extensive repairs, you might explore our other restorative dentistry services.

Benefits of Tooth Bonding for South Florida Patients

Same-Visit Results Without Removing Tooth Structure

Unlike crowns or veneers, bonding usually doesn’t require drilling or anesthetic. Your dentist roughens the tooth surface slightly, applies the resin, and sculpts it into place. The entire process often takes an hour or less, so you can walk out with a repaired smile the same day.

A Budget-Friendly Alternative to Veneers or Crowns

Dental bonding costs significantly less than porcelain veneers or crowns, making it a practical choice for many patients. While it may not last as long as those options, bonding offers an affordable way to improve your smile now. If you need more durable repairs, we also offer dental restorations and dental crowns.

Bonding vs. Veneers — Which Is Right for You?

Both bonding and veneers can improve the look of your teeth, but they differ in cost, durability, and preparation. Here’s a side-by-side comparison:

FeatureDental BondingVeneers
Treatment TimeOne visit, often under an hour per toothTwo or more visits over several weeks
Cost RangeLower – hundreds per toothHigher – typically $1,000+ per tooth
Tooth Prep RequiredMinimal – little to no enamel removalSome enamel removal needed
Durability/Lifespan3 to 10 years with care10 to 15 years or more
Best Suited ForMinor chips, gaps, and stainingLarger cosmetic changes, permanent results

If you’re considering a long-term smile upgrade, our veneers & smile makeovers may be a better fit. In many cases, bonding is a great first step to test a new look.

What to Expect During Your Dental Bonding Appointment

Step-by-Step: From Consultation to Finished Smile

  1. Consultation – Your dentist examines your teeth and discusses your goals. No prep work is needed beforehand.
  2. Shade Selection – A resin color is chosen to match your natural teeth.
  3. Preparation – The tooth surface is gently roughened to help the bond hold.
  4. Application – The resin is applied, molded, and sculpted to the desired shape.
  5. Curing – A special light hardens the material instantly.
  6. Finishing – Your dentist trims, polishes, and buffs the bonded area for a smooth, natural finish.

The whole appointment is comfortable and usually requires no numbing. Afterward, you can eat, drink, and go about your day right away.

For details on costs and coverage, visit our insurance & financing page.

What Is a Dental Bridge and Who Needs One?

A dental bridge is a custom tooth replacement that literally bridges the gap left by one or more missing teeth. It consists of a false tooth (called a pontic) held in place by crowns on the teeth next to the gap. Bridges are a great option when you have healthy teeth on both sides of the missing space.

You might be a good candidate if you are missing one to three teeth in a row and want a fixed, non-removable solution. For patients with more extensive tooth loss, our dental restorations include options like dentures and partials as well. Your dentist will help you choose the approach that fits your needs.

Benefits of Choosing a Dental Bridge for Missing Tooth Replacement

  • •Restores your ability to chew and speak without worrying about gaps.
  • •Prevents remaining teeth from shifting into the empty space.
  • •Maintains your facial shape by supporting lips and cheeks.
  • •Provides a natural appearance that blends with your surrounding teeth.
  • •Does not require surgery (unlike dental implants).
  • •Often completed in just two appointments, making it a convenient choice.

Dental Bridges vs. Dental Crowns: Which Is Right for You?

Both bridges and crowns restore damaged or missing teeth, but they serve different purposes. A crown covers a single damaged tooth, while a bridge replaces a missing tooth by using crowns on adjacent teeth. The table below compares the two.

FeatureDental BridgeDental Crown
PurposeReplaces a missing tooth by bridging the gapCovers and protects a damaged tooth
Number of teeth addressedOne or more missing teeth (plus anchoring teeth)One single tooth
Procedure lengthTwo appointments over a few weeksTwo appointments over a few weeks
Cost rangeHigher due to multiple crowns and ponticLower, since only one tooth is involved
Ideal candidatePatients with missing teeth and healthy adjacent teethPatients with a cracked, decayed, or weakened tooth
Longevity10–15 years with proper care10–15 years with proper care

If you are deciding between a bridge and a crown, your dentist at Riverwalk Dental Group will help you determine the best option. Learn more about dental crowns and how they compare.

What to Expect During Your Bridge Procedure

Your First Consultation and Treatment Plan

During your initial visit, we examine the area and take digital X-rays to see the health of your teeth and bone. Your dentist will discuss your goals and explain the bridge process. If you are ready to move forward, we prepare a treatment plan tailored to you.

Placement Appointments and Fitting Your Bridge

The first appointment involves carefully preparing the teeth on either side of the gap. We shape them to fit crowns, then take impressions of your teeth. A temporary bridge protects the area while your custom bridge is made. At your second visit, we remove the temporary and cement your permanent bridge in place. We make sure it looks natural and feels comfortable.

What Are Dental Restorations?

Dental restorations are treatments designed to repair or replace damaged tooth structure. They address common problems like cavities, chips, cracks, wear from grinding, and missing teeth. The goal is to restore function, comfort, and appearance so you can eat, speak, and smile with confidence. Whether you have a small cavity or a tooth that needs more support, our team will help you choose the right option.

Restoration Options We Offer across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter

We provide several types of restorations to match your needs. Each option is designed to return your tooth to full health and strength.

  • •Dental fillings across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter: We use tooth-colored composite fillings to treat cavities and minor damage. Fillings blend in with your natural tooth and can often be placed in a single visit.
  • •Dental crowns: For teeth that are more severely damaged, a custom crown can cover and protect the entire tooth. Crowns restore shape, size, and strength.
  • •Dental bridges: If you are missing one or more teeth, a bridge fills the gap using crowns on the adjacent teeth and an artificial tooth in between. This helps you chew properly and prevents teeth from shifting.
  • •Dental bonding: For chips, cracks, or gaps, bonding uses a tooth-colored resin to reshape and repair the tooth. It is a quick, affordable option that often takes just one visit.
  • •Dentures and partials: When multiple teeth are missing, removable dentures can restore your smile and your ability to eat comfortably.

Each option is tailored to your oral health. Our goal is to give you a natural-looking result that lasts.

Why Dental Restorations Matter for Your Oral Health

Restoring damaged teeth does more than improve your smile. It protects your overall health. A restored tooth allows you to chew food properly, which helps digestion. It also keeps surrounding teeth in their correct positions, reducing the risk of future problems. Restorations relieve pain from decay and prevent bacteria from spreading. By choosing the right restoration, you can avoid more complex treatments down the road.

What Happens If You Leave a Damaged Tooth Untreated?

Ignoring a damaged tooth can lead to bigger issues. Decay can reach the inner pulp, causing infection and the need for root canal therapy. Cracked teeth may worsen, leading to fractures that require extraction. When a tooth is missing, neighboring teeth can shift, creating bite problems and making cleaning harder. Acting early helps you avoid more extensive and expensive treatments. A simple filling today can save you from needing a crown or extraction later.

Dental Restorations vs. Dental Crowns: Which Do You Need?

Choosing between a general restoration and a crown depends on the condition of your tooth. The table below highlights the main differences.

FeatureDental Restorations (General)Dental Crowns
Best forCavities, chips, minor-to-moderate damageSeverely damaged, weakened, or root-canal-treated teeth
CoveragePartial tooth surfaceFull tooth cap
Common typesFillings, bonding, inlays/onlaysPorcelain, ceramic, zirconia crowns
Procedure visitsOften 1 visitTypically 2 visits
LongevityVaries by type (5–15+ years)10–15+ years average

If your tooth is still mostly intact, a filling or bonding may be enough. For teeth that are cracked or have had a root canal, a crown offers stronger protection. During your exam, we will recommend the option that best fits your situation. You can learn more on our dental crowns page.

What sets us apart is the depth of our team. In addition to experienced general dentists, we have endodontists, a periodontist, and an oral surgeon on staff. And if you are nervous about dental visits, our sedation options help you stay relaxed throughout your appointment. Our team takes the time to explain everything and make sure you feel at ease.

Common Dental Emergencies We Treat

Severe Tooth Pain and Toothaches

Sharp, throbbing, or constant tooth pain is a sign that something is wrong. It could be a cavity, an infection, or a cracked tooth. We will diagnose the cause and provide relief, whether that means a filling, root canal, or other treatment.

Broken, Chipped, or Cracked Teeth

A broken tooth can leave the inner layers exposed to bacteria and cause pain. Depending on the severity, we may repair it with bonding, a crown, or a more advanced restoration. Prompt treatment protects the tooth from further damage.

Knocked-Out or Dislodged Teeth

If a tooth is knocked out entirely, time is critical. Handle the tooth carefully, keep it moist, and come to our office immediately. We may be able to replant the tooth if we see you soon enough.

Lost Fillings, Crowns, or Dental Work

When a filling or crown falls out, the tooth beneath becomes vulnerable. We can replace the restoration and protect the tooth from decay or breakage. If you are in pain, we will address that too.

Dental Abscess or Swelling

An abscess is a pocket of infection that can cause swelling, fever, and severe pain. It requires immediate attention to prevent the infection from spreading. We will drain the abscess and treat the underlying cause, often with a root canal or extraction.

What Happens If You Wait? Understanding the Risks of Untreated Dental Emergencies

Waiting to treat a dental emergency can lead to serious consequences. The most immediate risk is infection spread. A small cavity or crack can allow bacteria to reach the pulp, causing an abscess that may spread to the jaw, neck, or bloodstream. This is not common but it is dangerous, so prompt care matters.

Another risk is tooth loss. Many emergency conditions, like a knocked-out tooth or deep fracture, can be successfully treated if you act quickly. Delaying reduces the chance of saving the natural tooth.

Untreated problems also become more complex over time. A simple filling can become a root canal, and a root canal can become an extraction. The longer you wait, the more involved (and costly) the treatment becomes.

Finally, there is the cost. A quick visit for a lost filling is far less expensive than a crown, root canal, or implant that may be needed after weeks of neglect. Treating emergencies promptly saves you time, discomfort, and money.

What to Expect at Your Emergency Dental Appointment

Your visit starts with a phone call or online booking. When you arrive, our team will see you quickly and ask about your symptoms. We will take X-rays if needed to understand what is happening. Then we will focus on pain relief first, whether that means numbing the area, prescribing medication, or performing a temporary fix.

Once you are comfortable, we will discuss treatment options and create a plan. Depending on the case, we may handle everything in one visit or schedule follow-up care. Our goal is to make the experience as calm and straightforward as possible. You will never feel rushed, and we will answer all your questions.

Signs You May Need a Root Canal

Tooth pain often signals that the nerve inside the tooth is infected or damaged. Common signs include:

  • •Sensitivity to hot or cold that lingers
  • •Darkening or discoloration of the tooth

Your endodontist will begin by numbing the area with local anesthesia. Once you are completely comfortable, they will create a small opening in the tooth to remove the infected pulp. Most patients return to work or school the same day or the next. You may have mild tenderness in the area for a few days, which is easily managed with over-the-counter pain relievers. Signs You May Need Gum Disease Treatment

Gum disease often develops quietly. Many people do not realize they have it until a dentist or periodontist spots the signs during a routine exam. Knowing the symptoms can help you seek care early.

Common Symptoms

  • •Bleeding gums: If your gums bleed when you brush or floss, it is often the first sign of inflammation.
  • •Receding gums: Teeth that look longer than usual or exposed roots may indicate gum recession.
  • •Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to hot or cold foods can mean your gums are pulling away from your teeth.
  • •Loose teeth: Advanced gum disease can weaken the bone that holds teeth in place.

Who Is at Risk?

Anyone can develop gum disease, but certain factors raise your chances. Smoking, diabetes, stress, genetics, and poor oral hygiene all play a role. Hormonal changes during pregnancy can also make gums more sensitive. If any of these apply to you, regular periodontal checkups are especially important.

Periodontal Treatments We Offer

We tailor treatment to match the severity of your gum disease. Less advanced cases often respond well to non-surgical care, while more serious conditions may require surgical intervention.

Scaling and Root Planing

This deep-cleaning procedure removes plaque and tartar from below the gum line. It smooths the root surfaces so your gums can reattach to your teeth. Scaling and root planing is the most common first step in periodontal treatment across Port St. Lucie, Saint Lucie West, Stuart, and Jupiter and is usually performed under local anesthesia for comfort.

Periodontal Maintenance

After initial treatment, you will need regular maintenance cleanings to keep gum disease from coming back. These visits happen every three to four months and focus on areas that are difficult to clean at home.

Surgical Periodontal Options

For more advanced cases, surgical procedures such as pocket reduction, gum grafting, or bone surgery may be needed. Dr. Gholami uses the latest techniques to restore the health and structure of your gums and supporting bone.

Privacy Policy

Effective Date: August 12, 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how this dental practice (“we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, shares, and protects information when you visit or interact with this website. We are committed to safeguarding your privacy and handling your personal information responsibly.

By using this website, you acknowledge that you have read and understand this Privacy Policy. If you do not agree with the practices described here, please do not use this website.

1. Information We Collect

We may collect the following categories of information when you visit or interact with this website:

1.1 Information You Provide Directly

When you submit a form, request an appointment, or otherwise contact us through this website, you may provide information such as:

  • •Your name
  • •Email address
  • •Phone number
  • •Appointment preferences or scheduling requests
  • •Any additional information you choose to include in a message or form submission

1.2 Information Collected Automatically

When you visit this website, certain information is collected automatically through cookies, scripts, and similar technologies. This may include:

  • •IP address and approximate geographic location
  • •Browser type, device type, and operating system
  • •Pages visited, time spent on pages, and navigation patterns
  • •Referring website or source that directed you to this site
  • •Phone call activity, including calls placed through dynamically displayed phone numbers on this website (used for call attribution and analytics purposes)

1.3 Information from Third-Party Tools

This website uses third-party analytics, advertising, and operational tools that may collect information about your activity. These tools are described in more detail in Section 4 (Cookies and Tracking Technologies) below.

2. How We Use Your Information

We use the information collected through this website for the following purposes:

  • •To respond to your inquiries, appointment requests, and form submissions
  • •To communicate with you regarding your request or our services
  • •To operate, maintain, and improve this website
  • •To analyze website traffic and user behavior for performance optimization
  • •To measure the effectiveness of advertising and marketing efforts
  • •To attribute phone calls and inquiries to their originating source for analytics purposes
  • •To comply with applicable legal obligations

3. How We Share Your Information

We do not sell your personal information. We may share your information in the following circumstances:

3.1 Website Management Provider

This website is operated and maintained by a third-party website management provider on behalf of this practice. This provider receives and processes form submissions, analytics data, and call tracking information in the course of managing this website. This provider processes your information on behalf of this practice for the purposes of website management and is not authorized to use your personal information for its own independent purposes.

3.2 Third-Party Service Providers

We use third-party tools and services for analytics, advertising, call tracking, and website functionality. These providers may collect or receive information about your activity on this website as described in Section 4. Examples of categories of service providers include:

  • •Website analytics providers
  • •Advertising and marketing platforms
  • •Call tracking and attribution services
  • •Form processing and delivery services

3.3 Legal Requirements

We may disclose your information if required to do so by law, regulation, legal process, or governmental request, or if we believe disclosure is necessary to protect our rights, your safety, or the safety of others.

4. Cookies and Tracking Technologies

This website uses cookies and similar tracking technologies to collect information about your browsing activity. These technologies serve different purposes:

4.1 Essential Cookies

These cookies are necessary for the basic operation of this website, such as enabling page navigation and access to secure areas. The website cannot function properly without these cookies.

4.2 Analytics Cookies

We use analytics tools to understand how visitors interact with this website. These tools collect information such as pages visited, time spent on site, and how visitors arrived at the site. This information is used to improve website performance and user experience.

4.3 Advertising and Marketing Cookies

This website may use advertising and remarketing technologies provided by third-party platforms. These tools may use cookies or tracking pixels to measure advertising effectiveness, deliver relevant advertisements on other websites or platforms, and track conversions from advertising campaigns.

4.4 Call Tracking Technology

This website uses dynamic number insertion technology that displays unique phone numbers to visitors for the purpose of attributing calls to their originating source (such as a specific advertising campaign or web page). This technology uses scripts to associate your browsing session with a displayed phone number and may collect information about the referring source and caller identification details.

4.5 Managing Your Cookie and Tracking Preferences

You can manage or disable cookies through your browser settings. Please note that disabling certain cookies may affect the functionality of this website. Most browsers allow you to refuse or delete cookies. Instructions for managing cookies vary by browser.

You may also opt out of interest-based advertising through the following methods:

  • •Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) opt-out tool at optout.aboutads.info
  • •Network Advertising Initiative (NAI) opt-out tool at optout.networkadvertising.org
  • •Adjusting your advertising preferences within the settings of platforms such as Google and Meta
  • •Using browser-based opt-out signals such as Global Privacy Control (GPC). Where required by applicable law, we honor GPC signals as a valid opt-out request for the sale or sharing of personal information. You can learn more about GPC at globalprivacycontrol.org

5. HIPAA and Protected Health Information (PHI)

This website is not a secure or HIPAA-compliant communication channel. The contact forms and general communication features on this website are not designed or intended for the transmission of Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Please do not submit sensitive health information, medical records, insurance details, Social Security numbers, or other Protected Health Information through the forms on this website.

If this practice offers online scheduling, patient intake forms, or other services that involve the collection of health-related information, those services are provided through separate, HIPAA-compliant third-party platforms and are governed by their own privacy policies and terms of use. Those platforms are independent of this website.

If you have questions about how your health information is handled by this practice, please contact the practice directly using the contact information provided on this website.

6. Medical Disclaimer

The content on this website is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. It is not intended to be, and should not be construed as, professional medical or dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

No Doctor-Patient Relationship. Visiting this website or submitting a form does not establish a doctor-patient relationship between you and this practice. A doctor-patient relationship is established only through a formal in-person or telehealth consultation as agreed upon by the provider.

Not a Substitute for Professional Care. You should not rely on information presented on this website as a substitute for professional dental or medical advice. Always seek the advice of a qualified healthcare provider with any questions you may have regarding a dental or medical condition.

No Guarantee of Results. Any descriptions of procedures, treatments, outcomes, or testimonials on this website are for informational purposes and do not guarantee specific results. Individual outcomes may vary.

7. Emergency Disclaimer

If you are experiencing a medical or dental emergency, call 911 or go to your nearest emergency room immediately. Do not use this website, its forms, or any communication feature on this website to seek emergency care. This website is not monitored for urgent or time-sensitive communications.

8. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on where you reside, you may have certain rights regarding your personal information under applicable state privacy laws. This section describes those rights and how to exercise them.

8.1 Rights Under California Law (CCPA / CPRA)

If you are a California resident, you may have the following rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA):

  • •Right to Know: You may request that we disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal information we have collected about you, the categories of sources from which it was collected, the purposes for collection, and the categories of third parties with whom it was shared.
  • •Right to Delete: You may request that we delete personal information we have collected from you, subject to certain exceptions.
  • •Right to Correct: You may request that we correct inaccurate personal information we maintain about you.
  • •Right to Opt-Out of Sale or Sharing: We do not sell your personal information. To the extent that our use of third-party advertising technologies may constitute “sharing” of personal information under the CCPA, you have the right to opt out of such sharing. You may exercise this right by adjusting your cookie and tracking preferences as described in Section 4.5 of this Privacy Policy, including by using a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal in your browser.
  • •Right to Non-Discrimination: We will not discriminate against you for exercising any of your privacy rights.

8.2 Rights Under Other State Privacy Laws

Residents of states with comprehensive privacy laws, including but not limited to Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, and other states that have enacted consumer privacy legislation, may have similar rights, including the right to access, correct, or delete personal information, and the right to opt out of certain data processing activities such as targeted advertising.

If you wish to exercise any of these rights, please contact this practice using the contact information provided on this website. We will respond to verifiable requests within the timeframes required by applicable law. We may need to verify your identity before processing your request.

9. International Visitors

This website is operated in the United States and is intended for visitors located in the United States. If you are visiting this website from outside the United States, please be aware that your information may be transferred to, stored, and processed in the United States, where data protection laws may differ from those in your country of residence.

By using this website, you acknowledge and consent to the transfer of your information to the United States. If you do not consent to this transfer, please do not use this website. If you are located in the European Economic Area (EEA), United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with data protection laws, you may have additional rights regarding your personal information. Please contact this practice using the contact information provided on this website to exercise those rights.

10. Data Retention

We retain personal information collected through this website for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described in this Privacy Policy, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law. Form submissions and related communications are retained for a reasonable period to facilitate follow-up and practice operations. Aggregated or anonymized data that cannot be used to identify you may be retained indefinitely for analytical purposes.

11. Data Security

We implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect the information collected through this website from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is completely secure. While we strive to protect your information, we cannot guarantee absolute security.

In the event of a data breach that affects your personal information, we will notify affected individuals and applicable regulatory authorities as required by law.

12. Children’s Privacy

This website is not directed at children under the age of 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you are a parent or guardian and believe that your child has provided personal information through this website, please contact us using the contact information provided on this website so that we can take appropriate steps to delete that information.

13. Third-Party Links

This website may contain links to third-party websites, platforms, or services, including but not limited to online scheduling platforms, patient intake systems, social media pages, and review sites. These third-party services are not operated or controlled by this practice, and their use is governed by their own privacy policies and terms of use. We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of third-party websites.

14. How to Contact Us

If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, wish to exercise your privacy rights, or have concerns about how your information is handled, please contact this practice using the contact information provided on this website.

15. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices, technology, legal requirements, or other factors. When we make material changes, we will update the “Effective Date” at the top of this policy. We encourage you to review this Privacy Policy periodically to stay informed about how your information is being protected.

Accessibility Statement

Effective Date: August 12, 2026

1. Our Commitment

This dental practice is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for all visitors, including individuals with disabilities. We have invested in the design and development of this website with the goal of providing an accessible and usable experience for all users, and we are continually working to maintain and improve the accessibility of this website.

2. Accessibility Standards

This website has been designed with accessibility in mind and targets conformance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA, as published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). These guidelines define how to make web content more accessible to people with a wide range of disabilities, including visual, auditory, physical, speech, cognitive, language, learning, and neurological disabilities.

3. Measures to Support Accessibility

This practice takes the following measures to support and maintain the accessibility of this website:

  • •Incorporate accessibility considerations into our website design, development, and content management processes
  • •Conduct periodic reviews of this website against applicable accessibility standards
  • •Provide accessibility guidance and training to those responsible for website content and development
  • •Address reported accessibility barriers in a timely and reasonable manner

4. Third-Party Content

This website may incorporate content, features, or functionality provided by third-party services, including but not limited to online scheduling platforms, patient intake portals, payment processors, review platforms, and embedded maps. While we encourage our third-party service providers to adhere to applicable accessibility standards, content and functionality provided by third parties are not under our direct control and may not conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA in all respects.

Additionally, certain content such as user-submitted reviews, testimonials, or uploaded documents (including PDF files) may present accessibility limitations. If you require access to information contained in any content on this website that is not accessible to you, please contact this practice using the contact information provided on this website and we will work with you to provide the information in an alternative format.

5. Accessibility Feedback

We value feedback from all visitors regarding the accessibility of this website. If you experience difficulty accessing any content, feature, or functionality on this website, or if you have suggestions for improvement, please contact this practice using the contact information provided on this website. When reporting an accessibility concern, please include:

  • •A description of the accessibility issue or barrier you encountered
  • •The web page address (URL) or location where the issue occurred
  • •Your contact information so that we may follow up with you

We will make reasonable efforts to respond to accessibility feedback and to address reported barriers.

6. Alternative Means of Access

If you are unable to access any content, feature, or functionality on this website due to a disability, please contact this practice directly using the contact information provided on this website. We are committed to providing the information, services, or functionality you seek through an alternative means of communication or format that is accessible to you.
